content.title: Process Proof | Material Coverage as Progress
content.summary: The same craft object remains continuous, using a material variable that only increases and never decreases as a clear progress indicator.

quick_start.input_format: The same craft object + a material variable that only increases and never decreases + 4 stages + the finished product is revealed
quick_start.recommended_input: The same ceramic relief remains on the turntable as glaze coverage expands monotonically from the edges, through the recessed texture, to the full surface. End with the finished relief revealed in kiln-fire reflection.
required_anchors: The same craft object is consistent throughout
Selected material variables only increase and never decrease
Finally, the finished product is clearly revealed
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: The same craft object remains continuous, using material variables that only increase but not decrease as a clear progress clock.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Compress a multi-stage making process around one persistent artifact and one irreversible visual variable that only increases—coverage, polish, oxidation, translucency or revealed pattern. Alternate contact-level macro proof with scale-restoring views, ensure each cut advances the same artifact, and reserve the longest hold for the completed state. Craft, object, material, palette, stage count and final display are variable.

invariants.rule: Establish one artifact in an unadvanced base state.
invariants.purpose: Creates the zero point for the visual clock.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a base state, progress cannot be measured.

invariants.rule: Keep object identity and defining geometry stable across process cuts.
invariants.purpose: Lets the viewer accumulate changes on one artifact.
invariants.ablation_failure: Object swaps look like unrelated demonstrations.

invariants.rule: Advance one irreversible material variable in a single direction.
invariants.purpose: Turns coverage into an intuitive timeline.
invariants.ablation_failure: Reversing or resetting the variable breaks progress.

invariants.rule: Show direct tool-to-material contact at each key state change.
invariants.purpose: Provides causal proof and tactile credibility.
invariants.ablation_failure: Off-screen transformations feel like magic rather than craft.

invariants.rule: Give the finished artifact a longer clean hold after the final operation.
invariants.purpose: Rewards the compressed process and confirms completion.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending during the last tool action denies the payoff.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original subject whose identity and silhouette remain stable.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific location.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One readable variable that changes monotonically or in countable stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: One restrained performance rule that makes the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A coherent information order that does not copy the source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: One clean physical or graphic consequence that closes the causal chain.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: A new hierarchy of diegetic cues supporting each state change.

anti_copy_exclusions: red bulbous vase with raised coiled dragon-like relief
gold leaf applied over red lacquer
source artisan face, workshop and exact tool sequence

instantiations.concept: A ceramic relief tile progresses from pale bisque through carved channels to increasing translucent teal glaze coverage, final kiln gloss and a clean gallery reveal.
instantiations.prompt_seed: Macro ceramic process using teal glaze coverage as the irreversible visual clock.

instantiations.concept: A wooden music-box lid moves from raw carving to increasing blue resin inlay, sanding, polish and a reflective final pattern.
instantiations.prompt_seed: One persistent lid with blue inlay coverage growing across every cut.

instantiations.concept: A copper botanical plaque advances from clean metal through wax masking to spreading green patina, selective polish and final framed display.
instantiations.prompt_seed: Patina coverage is the monotonic progress variable across a tactile metal process.

failure_modes.failure: Different objects appear at different stages.
failure_modes.repair: Lock one artifact silhouette, motif and scale across every cut.

failure_modes.failure: Coverage jumps backward or changes hue randomly.
failure_modes.repair: Choose one irreversible variable and make every cut advance it.

failure_modes.failure: Only finished beauty shots are shown.
failure_modes.repair: Include direct tool contact and readable intermediate states before the final hold.
